top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Majka Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before August.
Majka Gran Fondo's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Surge over the rough stuff, settle on the smooth, repeat for 53 miles.
5,200ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
97ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
At Majka Gran Fondo, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Majka Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.
53 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
5,200ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Majka Gran Fondo, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
Short, max efforts are unavoidable. Punchy climbs, gap closures, attacks on mixed terrain. If you haven't trained them, you'll crack.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 5,200ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Low-cadence force work for 5,200ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for Majka Gran Fondo’s 53 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum; adjust for conditions and sweat rate.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Majka Gran Fondo requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, Gravel Specific, and VO2max to prepare you for 53 miles of mixed terrain in Krakow, Poland.
